title: Normalized derived cohomology comparisons for exact functors and their composites
statement:
Let $\mathcal A,\mathcal B,\mathcal C$ be abelian categories [def-sp-abelian], and let $F:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ and $G:\mathcal B\to\mathcal C$ be exact functors (additive and preserving finite limits and finite colimits). Use ordinary unbounded derived categories, defined by localization of cochain complexes at quasi-isomorphisms [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and write $H^a$ for the induced cohomology functors, $a\in\mathbf Z$. Let $DF,DG,D(GF)$ be their termwise induced derived functors [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated]. There is a canonical isomorphism
$$ \theta^a_{F,K}:F(H^aK)\xrightarrow{\sim}H^a(DFK) $$
for every $K\in D(\mathcal A)$, natural for every morphism of the derived category. On each cochain complex representative its map is the inverse of the comparison induced by preservation of kernels, images and quotients, transported through the localization factorizations. In particular, it is independent of the representative. Let $c_K:D(GF)K\xrightarrow{\sim}DG(DFK)$ be the derived compositor induced by the termwise identity. Then
$$ H^a(c_K)\circ\theta^a_{GF,K}=\theta^a_{G,DFK}\circ G(\theta^a_{F,K}). $$
More generally, for an exact $L:\mathcal A\to\mathcal C$ and a natural isomorphism $\eta:GF\xrightarrow{\sim}L$, let $d:DG\circ DF\xrightarrow{\sim}DL$ be the natural isomorphism $d_K=(D\eta)_K\circ c_K^{-1}$, the inverse of the compositor followed by $D\eta$. The same normalized comparisons satisfy
$$ H^a(d_K)\circ\theta^a_{G,DFK}\circ G(\theta^a_{F,K})=\theta^a_{L,K}\circ\eta_{H^aK}. $$
All assertions hold for arbitrary unbounded complexes, with no resolution or boundedness hypothesis.

proof.text:
Fix $a\in\mathbf Z$. For a cochain complex $C$ write $i_C:Z_C=\ker d_C^a\hookrightarrow C^a$ and $p_C:Z_C\twoheadrightarrow H^a(C)$. By [lem-sp-exact-functor-preserves-homology], exactness gives the kernel isomorphism $z_{F,C}:FZ_C\xrightarrow{\sim}Z_{FC}$ with $i_{FC}z_{F,C}=F(i_C)$, and the inverse homology comparison $t_{F,C}:FH^a(C)\xrightarrow{\sim}H^a(FC)$ characterized by
$$t_{F,C}F(p_C)=p_{FC}z_{F,C}.$$
It is natural for cochain maps by clause (c) of that node. In particular, for a quasi-isomorphism $u$, $H^a(Fu)=t_{F,C'}F(H^a(u))t_{F,C}^{-1}$ is invertible, for every $a$. This checks the quasi-isomorphism hypothesis needed below, without boundedness.

source.place: Tag 010N, lemma-exact-functor, kernel/cokernel proof; its homology consequence in lem-sp-exact-functor-preserves-homology (c).

proof.text:
Let $Q_{\mathcal A},Q_{\mathcal B}$ be the complex localizations of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and write $\lambda_{\mathcal A,C}:H^a(Q_{\mathcal A}C)\xrightarrow{\sim}H^a(C)$ for the cohomology factorization. The termwise derived functor of [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated] has its localization comparison $\sigma_{F,C}:DF(Q_{\mathcal A}C)\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_{\mathcal B}(FC)$. The two functors $H^a(DF(-))$ and $F(H^a(-))$, restricted along $Q_{\mathcal A}$, are identified with the two cochain functors of Step 1. Clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] therefore lifts $t_F$ uniquely to a natural isomorphism $\theta_F^a$, with
$$\theta^a_{F,Q_{\mathcal A}C}=H^a(\sigma_{F,C})^{-1}\lambda_{\mathcal B,FC}^{-1}t_{F,C}F(\lambda_{\mathcal A,C}).$$
Both restricted functors invert quasi-isomorphisms by Step 1 and the definition of $H^a$. The uniqueness is among natural transformations on the entire derived category. Thus naturality holds for all derived morphisms and the formula is independent of any representative or representing isomorphism. Apply the same construction to $G,GF,L$.

source.place: Tag 015F, lemma-right-derived-exact-functor, termwise unbounded descent; agent-written normalized natural-transformation lift using the cited localization node.

proof.text:
The cochain composition equation follows directly from Step 1. The two maps from $GFZ_C$ to $Z_{GFC}$ satisfy
$$i_{GFC}z_{GF,C}=GF(i_C)=i_{GFC}z_{G,FC}G(z_{F,C}),$$
so cancel the kernel monomorphism to get $z_{GF,C}=z_{G,FC}G(z_{F,C})$. Consequently
$$t_{GF,C}GF(p_C)=p_{GFC}z_{GF,C}=t_{G,FC}G(t_{F,C})GF(p_C).$$
Cancel the epimorphism $GF(p_C)$, which is epic by [lem-sp-exact-functor-preserves-homology] (a) applied successively to $F$ and $G$. This gives $t_{GF,C}=t_{G,FC}G(t_{F,C})$. Lean implementation: apply the existing proved source-library ShortComplex.mapHomologyIso_comp to the short complex in degree a, identify its hom with mapHomologicalComplexHomologyIso_hom_app_eq, and take inverses. The cited composition lemma proves precisely this kernel-mono and homology-epi cancellation.

source.place: Tag 010N, lemma-exact-functor; elementary uniqueness of the kernel map and cancellation of the preserved quotient epimorphism.

proof.text:
The termwise identity $(GF)C=G(FC)$ lifts by clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] to the compositor $c:D(GF)\xrightarrow{\sim}DG\circ DF$, characterized by
$$\sigma_{G,FC}\,DG(\sigma_{F,C})\,c_{Q_{\mathcal A}C}=\sigma_{GF,C}.$$
Consider the two natural transformations $H^a(c)\theta^a_{GF}$ and $\theta^a_{G,DF(-)}G(\theta^a_F)$. On $Q_{\mathcal A}C$, substitute the formula of Step 2 and the displayed characterization of $c$; naturality of $\theta_G$ for $\sigma_{F,C}$ moves its evaluation from $DF(Q_{\mathcal A}C)$ to $Q_{\mathcal B}(FC)$. Cancelling the adjacent $\sigma$ and $\lambda$ isomorphisms reduces their equality to $t_{GF,C}=t_{G,FC}G(t_{F,C})$, proved in Step 3. Clause (3) of the cited localization node now gives their equality on $D(\mathcal A)$. Lean implementation: use mapDerivedCategoryCompIso_fac, cancel the termwise identity, solve for sigma_GF inverse followed by c by cancelling the other factorization isomorphisms, and use mapDerivedCategoryHomologyFunctorIso_hom_app_Q. Apply naturality of theta_G along sigma_F inverse, cancel lambda_B inverse followed by lambda_B, and use Step 3. Localization.natTrans_ext supplies clause (3).

source.place: Tag 015F, lemma-right-derived-exact-functor; agent-written compositor normalization and localization equality argument.

proof.text:
For $\eta:GF\xrightarrow{\sim}L$, let $\eta_C:(GF)C\to LC$ be the termwise cochain map. Naturality of $\eta$ for $i_C$ and cancellation of $i_{LC}$ give
$$Z(\eta_C)z_{GF,C}=z_{L,C}\eta_{Z_C}.$$
Here $Z(\eta_C)$ is the map induced on kernels; its defining equation is $i_{LC}Z(\eta_C)=\eta_{C^a}i_{GFC}$. By the definition of the induced homology map, $H^a(\eta_C)p_{GFC}=p_{LC}Z(\eta_C)$. Hence
$$H^a(\eta_C)t_{GF,C}GF(p_C)=p_{LC}z_{L,C}\eta_{Z_C}=t_{L,C}L(p_C)\eta_{Z_C}=t_{L,C}\eta_{H^a(C)}GF(p_C).$$
The middle equality is Step 1 for $L$, and the last is naturality of $\eta$ for $p_C$. Cancel the epic $GF(p_C)$, using [lem-sp-exact-functor-preserves-homology] (a). This proves the cochain natural-isomorphism equation, with the specified comparison rather than an arbitrary isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 010N, lemma-exact-functor; elementary kernel and quotient universal properties and naturality of eta.

proof.text:
Clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] lifts the termwise $\eta_C$ to $D\eta:D(GF)\xrightarrow{\sim}DL$, with
$$\sigma_{L,C}(D\eta)_{Q_{\mathcal A}C}=Q_{\mathcal C}(\eta_C)\sigma_{GF,C}.$$
Substitute the Step 2 formulas for $\theta_{GF}$ and $\theta_L$ on $Q_{\mathcal A}C$. The displayed equation cancels the derived-functor factors, naturality of $\lambda_{\mathcal C}$ replaces $H^a(Q_{\mathcal C}(\eta_C))$ by $H^a(\eta_C)$, and naturality of $\eta$ for $\lambda_{\mathcal A,C}$ replaces the input coefficient factor. The remaining equality is exactly $H^a(\eta_C)t_{GF,C}=t_{L,C}\eta_{H^a(C)}$ from Step 5. Clause (3) gives
$$H^a((D\eta)_K)\theta^a_{GF,K}=\theta^a_{L,K}\eta_{H^aK}$$
for all derived $K$. Lean implementation: the existing proved source-library mapDerivedCategoryHomologyFunctorIso_hom_app_naturality already performs the cochain calculation and this descent for any natural isomorphism between exact functors. Specialize it to eta : F followed by G isomorphic to L.

source.place: Tag 015F, lemma-right-derived-exact-functor; agent-written descent of the explicitly proved natural-isomorphism equation.

proof.text:
By Step 4, $\theta^a_{G,DFK}G(\theta^a_{F,K})=H^a(c_K)\theta^a_{GF,K}$. Since $d_K=(D\eta)_Kc_K^{-1}$, functoriality of $H^a$ and $c_K^{-1}c_K=1$ give
$$H^a(d_K)\theta^a_{G,DFK}G(\theta^a_{F,K})=H^a((D\eta)_K)\theta^a_{GF,K}=\theta^a_{L,K}\eta_{H^aK},$$
where the last equality is Step 6. Every construction used only the three consecutive terms defining $H^a$ and the unbounded localization; no resolution or boundedness condition was introduced.
